children.text: The digital nomad visa is a special permit that allows you to live and travel abroad while working online.

Portugal is one of the most sought-after choices for digital nomads. If you love Portugal too - its unique culture, seaside cities, and stunning nature — and you work online, then you should definitely know why it's worth getting a digital nomad visa. And if you're looking for a comfortable, inspiring environment to work in, Portugal is an ideal choice for digital nomads!
Stay with us and find out about the advantages the nomad visa offers in Portugal.
The Right to Live Legally

The digital nomad visa allows you to live in Portugal for at least 1 year, whereas without a visa, you're only permitted to stay in the country for a maximum of 90 days within a six-month period. In addition, if you apply for the long-term visa, you'll be able to extend it, opening the path toward citizenship and permanent residency.
The Opportunity to Obtain European Citizenship

As a digital nomad, you have the opportunity to obtain a Portuguese passport if you spend more than five years in the country while integrating into the local culture. However, before obtaining citizenship, you must pass a language test at a minimum A2 level.
After obtaining EU citizenship, you'll be able to move, study, live, and work without restrictions in the EU's 27 countries, as well as in Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Switzerland.
Access to Government Services
As a holder of the digital nomad visa, you'll have the opportunity to use government services such as education, healthcare, and other social services.
While living legally, you'll be able to open bank accounts, use the local and international fiscal system, and enter into rental agreements.

Holders of the digital nomad visa can register with Portugal's National Health Service (SNS – Serviço Nacional de Saúde) and receive medical services, including free or low-cost consultations, emergency care, and hospital services.
The Opportunity to Give Citizenship to Your Newborn

If a child is born while in Portugal, as long as their parent holds residency rights, the newborn will automatically become a citizen of Portugal, with the exception that the parent must have lived in Portugal for at least 1 year.
The Right to Bring Family Members

The long-term nomad visa allows you to bring family members to live with you in Portugal, such as a spouse, unmarried children under 18, and parents over 65. Children over 18 and parents under 65 can only be brought if they are financially dependent on you.

If you want to work remotely, live in seaside cities, take advantage of EU government services, and create a comfortable environment for both yourself and your family members - Portugal's digital nomad visa is the ideal choice!
